extracted.intended_audience: theatre practitioners, critics, students of drama, and informed readers of Ibsen
extracted.subtask_description: Critical-evaluative criteria for assessing a late-19th-century realist play (Ibsen's Ghosts) with attention to technique, characterization, thematic daring, and stage-performance implications. Useful for critics, directors, playwrights, and scholars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial intrusion / absence of author's voice
rubrics_metrics.description: The very method, the order of technique which imposes its form upon the play, forbids the author to appear in the speeches of his characters; the author is external to the action, entirely absent from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid making the author responsible for opinions expressed by characters. Keep the author's private opinions out of the dialogue so the audience experiences the action as real. Anti-pattern: characters that clearly voice the author's personal doctrines or editorialising intrusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of preaching; dramatic neutrality toward doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: The play is 'not concerned to preach anything whatsoever. It merely points to the ferment of Nihilism going on under the surface...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present social or ideological conditions (e.g., 'ferment of Nihilism') without turning the drama into a sermon. The work should illustrate consequences and conflicts rather than explicitly advocate a doctrine. Anti-pattern: characters as mouthpieces for explicit doctrinal claims presented as the author's view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verisimilitude — making the reader/audience feel 'real experience'
rubrics_metrics.description: Ibsen's object: 'to make the reader feel that he was going through a piece of real experience.' He applies a new technical method to achieve this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use technical devices (structure, dialogue, staging) that create the sense of authentic lived experience. Prioritise concreteness and causal plausibility over theatrical artifice when the aim is realistic immersion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character complexity versus typification
rubrics_metrics.description: Some personages (Mrs. Alving, Engstrand, Regina) are 'rounded and breathing characters', while others (Manders) strike one 'as a clerical type rather than an individual.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for characters who feel individually known and psychologically rounded. Avoid flattening important figures into mere social or moral types unless intentional for thematic effect. Example anti-pattern: major figures who function only as exemplars (e.g., 'a clerical type') with little individual interiority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pace, variety and suppleness of action
rubrics_metrics.description: The action 'moves a little stiffly, and all in one rhythm. It lacks variety and suppleness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the play's movement has varied tempo, dramatic reliefs, and rhythmic flexibility so it does not feel monotonous. Structure scenes and beats to provide contrast and elasticity in dramatic energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between idea-driven (prosaic) method and poetic/human richness
rubrics_metrics.description: Ibsen is said to be 'under the sway of a prosaic ideal' and to have 'put some constraint upon the poet within him', giving rise to criticisms of being more of a preacher than a creator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a balance: allow intellectual/idea-driven ambitions to be embodied in human complexity and poetic richness. Avoid letting theoretical aims displace the humane and aesthetic qualities that make characters and scenes emotionally resonant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plausibility and factual/verifiable basis of pivotal incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions arise about whether Oswald's 'case' actually appears in medical books; Archer considers this 'of very trifling moment' so long as the presentation is 'typically true.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dramatizing specific conditions or technical facts, either ensure factual plausibility or demonstrate that the depiction is defensible as a representative/typical instance. If scientific or factual detail is central, provide believable grounding or acknowledge poetic licence. Anti-pattern: relying on striking but implausible specifics without narrative justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and importance of symbolic elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The prominence given to the uninsured Asylum is noted as having 'some symbolical purport; but ... it is not either sufficiently clear or sufficiently important to justify the emphasis.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbols and repeated motifs must be both clear in their intended resonance and justified in importance to the drama's economy; avoid overemphasising a symbol whose meaning or necessity is obscure to the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility of character actions and susceptibility to being victimised
rubrics_metrics.description: A blemish: 'the inconceivable facility with which, in the third act, Manders suffers himself to be victimised by Engstrand.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Character actions must follow believable psychological logic; avoid plot turns that make a character act in ways that seem out of character merely to serve contrivance. If a character is to be manipulated, stage clear causal motivations and preceding conditions that render it credible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of expressed motivations and argumentative lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Oswald's argument comparing the expensiveness of marriage and free union is criticised as 'never adequately explained, either as a matter of economic fact, or as a trait of character.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that important utterances that reveal character or social critique are either factually plausible or clearly motivated by the speaker's psychology and background. Avoid leaving pivotal lines unexplained or unanchored in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic completeness and avoidance of small cumulative flaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Several small flaws (suddenness of catastrophe, prominence of uninsured Asylum, unexplained arguments) 'taken together ... detract ... from the artistic completeness of the play.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to minor inconsistencies and loose ends as they can collectively undermine a play's overall artistic integrity. Edit and revise to tighten causal chains, symbolic clarity, and character motivation so that small blemishes do not aggregate into a major defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and influence — moving 'boundary-posts'
rubrics_metrics.description: Historically significant for giving 'the full measure of his technical and spiritual originality and daring' and for having 'advanced the frontiers of dramatic art and implanted new ideals.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess a work for its innovation in technique and thought and for its capacity to shift critical and artistic norms. Original departures from convention are valued when they convincingly open new expressive possibilities rather than merely shock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic daring and willingness to address taboo or socially sensitive issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The play was 'rather daring' and called forth a 'terrible uproar' and censorship in some countries; Ibsen intended 'to move some boundary-posts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether tackling contentious themes is handled with artistic responsibility and whether the daring serves insight rather than provocation for its own sake. Consider likely public/stage reception and possible censorship implications when producing or presenting such works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stageability, public acceptability and censorship risk
rubrics_metrics.description: The play's production history includes refusals by leading theatres, private performances, and a continuing public performance ban in England (as of 1906).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing a production, consider whether the content will provoke censorship or public backlash and how that affects staging choices, publicity, and legal/performance strategy. Anti-pattern: ignoring likely public/legal constraints on performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact versus popularity — distinction between influence and immediate appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Though not one of Ibsen's most popular plays, Ghosts is seen as epoch-making and extremely influential in its technical and intellectual effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between a work's immediate popular reception and its long-term artistic influence. A play may be historically important despite limited contemporary popularity; evaluation should weigh both immediate effect and enduring contribution.
